general_editor.notes: Strong structure: data hook → baseline argument → crop-level → economic → counterargument → limitations → actionable. 3,152 words appropriate for depth. Original caloric math adds genuine novel analysis. Opening Niño3.4 data point immediately establishes authority.

voice_coach.notes: All rhythm gates pass (variance 202.5, short 14.1%, long 62.5%). Em dashes: 2. Banned phrases: 0. 'The' starters: 1.7%. Good punch sentences ('Crops simply wilt.', 'Seven trillion dollars.', 'They always are.'). Reads like journalism, not AI summary. A few data-heavy transitions are functional rather than fluid.

ethics_reviewer.notes: No self-congratulation. Presents data and lets reader conclude. Honest limitations section. Fair counterargument. 'The people who cannot substitute are the poorest' is grounded in economic fact, not moral grandstanding. No savior complex. Attribution is fair to all sources.

social_shareability.notes: Strong pull quotes: '$3-7 trillion', '12-21 million person-years', 'societies do not just take a hit and recover'. Scale-shock numbers drive sharing. 'What You Can Do' section gives readers reason to forward. Long read may reduce casual mobile sharing. Topic is niche (El Niño) vs broad-appeal subjects.

legal_accuracy.notes: All citations to published sources (BoM, NOAA, IMD, USDA, Reuters, Citigroup, Callahan-Mankin 2023 Science paper). India 2023 export ban accurately described. No defamation risk. No legal claims requiring case law. Reuters farmer quotes properly attributed.

research_rigor.notes: Original caloric math is transparent and replicable. Baseline compounding argument is novel. Limitations honestly stated (2-datapoint nonlinear extrapolation, monsoon forecast volatility, substitution effects). Counterargument is fair. '15-25% yield reduction from halved nitrogen' cited as 'field-level agronomic studies' without specific papers — minor gap.

data_presentation.notes: Table used effectively for country-level risk breakdown. Key numbers anchored to human scale (Portugal population, Bangladesh fraction). Person-years denomination is accessible. Base rates included throughout (541 MT, India 28%). Comparison framing: 1997 vs 2026 baseline. Every major number passes 'so what?' test.
